title: Consent rules — media, voice, likeness, symptom language
appliesTo: Symptom language and clinical telemetry excerpts

principles.rule: The emergency may teach clinical mechanics. Rohan’s identity, voice, and authored framing require consent.
Do not clone a real child’s voice without consent. Use a licensed performer or an explicitly authorised synthetic voice.
Do not use the likeness of a real minor. Commissioned art and placeholders must remain fictional or fully licensed.
Personalised symptom language (for example RIGHT LOW, DEEP, RIGHT MIDDLE) is clinical communication belonging to Rohan’s authorship. It is not free promotional copy.
Raw AAC logs and private conversations are not routine evidence or marketing content.
A public location does not make a medical crisis public property. Recording should stop during deterioration; audience filming is restricted; emergency footage is not automatic training content.
Training packages that strip communication access, delirium, restraint review, school exclusion, home staffing, or privacy require renewed consent. Rohan may withdraw his name from shortened cuts.
Family fear is treated seriously. It does not authorise continuous bedroom video, GPS, or seizure of Rohan’s body and privacy as the treatment site for someone else’s trauma.
Simulation media never forced-autoplays. Captions, transcripts, audio description or descriptive text, pause/replay, and reduced-sensory alternatives are required for production paths.

productionChecklist: Confirm voice licence path before recording AAC lines
Confirm illustration licence or placeholder-only status
Keep symptom language attributed and reversible
Offer reduced-sensory alternate for any alarm-containing audio/video
Document withdrawals of consent in authorshipControl domain notes
